earlier_scan.source_named: Zöllner, Siegfried, ms. grammar of Angguruk Yali (unpublished, cited in the 2021 ANU dictionary). Read Riesberg's grammatical sketch + phonology in Zöllner et al. 2021 (ANU A-PL 37): no stress statement in it.

sources.citation: Zöllner, Siegfried & Ilse Zöllner; ed. Sonja Riesberg. 2021. A Yali (Angguruk) – English – German dictionary: Wörterbuch Yali (Angguruk) – Englisch – Deutsch. Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics, A-PL 40. 301 pp. ISBN 978-1-922185-42-6. hdl.handle.net/1885/127381 (ANU Open Research, CC BY 4.0). Intro = Riesberg's 'short grammatical sketch' (sections 1–4, pp. 1–48).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 3 'Phonology and orthography' (pp. 8–12: 3.1 consonant phonemes and allophones, 3.2 vowel phonemes, 3.3 orthographic notes) read in full: nothing on stress, accent, prosody, tone or intonation. Whole-text a full-text search for stress/accent/suprasegm/intonation/tone/pitch gives only non-phonological hits ('stress the fact', 'stone', 'higher pitch' in a song gloss). Note: the earlier scan and Glottolog call this A-PL 37; the 2021 edition is A-PL 40 (A-PL 37 is the 2017 Yali–German edition).

sources.note: Only full-length grammar of any Yali variety (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a grammar); a Leiden dissertation of this period normally opens with a phonology chapter that would state stress placement. Describes Abenaho (Pass Valley) Yali [yac], glottocode pass1247, so it would need an identity note if used for angg1239.
